summary: Feed s159_double is degraded: 26.3% duplicates (1085/4127 packets) exceeds 5% threshold and 91.7% encrypted bytes exceeds NDR 90% tolerance. Duplication corrupts NDR analysis; encryption limits payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Traffic is being delivered twice - classic double-feed from aggregating two SPAN/TAP sources covering the same link or a packet broker aggregation loop without deduplication. 1085 of 4127 packets (26.29%) are exact duplicates.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes 10G capacity processing duplicates, inflates flow/connection counts, breaks TCP reassembly and sequence tracking, causes false anomaly alerts and can exhaust state tables leading to missed detections.

recommended_fix.why: Enable hardware deduplication on the packet broker egress to s159_double to drop identical packets within a short time window before delivery, restoring correct packet counts and TCP state for the NDR.

findings.root_cause: 91.7% of bytes are encrypted (TLS), just above the NDR's 90% tolerance. Feed is almost entirely opaque without decryption - expected for modern traffic but exceeds what this NDR can handle without help.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload for signature and anomaly detection; at 92% encrypted it is largely blind to payloads and limited to metadata/JA3/flow analysis, reducing detection coverage for exploits and C2.

recommended_fix.why: Advise enabling selective TLS decryption / SSL visibility appliance before the packet broker or forwarding session keys so the NDR receives decrypted payload where policy allows; otherwise retune NDR to encrypted-traffic analytics and accept reduced payload detection.
